description: The bar charts compare the accuracy (%) of six different model variants—“Ours,” “w/o comments,” “w/o text,” “w/o select,” “w/o emotion,” and “w/o cognition”—on two misinformation detection datasets: PHEME (left) and PolitiFact (right). The vertical axis represents accuracy on a linear scale from 75.0% to 95.0%, marked at 2.5% intervals. In the PHEME chart, “Ours” achieves the highest accuracy at 89.84% (dark red bar), followed by “w/o select” at 88.80% (light blue), “w/o emotion” at 87.34% (medium blue), and “w/o cognition” at 87.17% (dark blue); “w/o comments” scores 86.82% (orange), while “w/o text” drops sharply to 80.10% (yellow), the lowest in this chart. In the PolitiFact chart, “Ours” again leads at 90.57% (dark red), followed by “w/o select” at 89.62% (light blue), “w/o cognition” at 87.74% (dark blue), “w/o emotion” at 84.91% (medium blue), “w/o comments” at 85.85% (orange), and “w/o text” at 83.02% (yellow), again the lowest. The consistent drop in performance when text is removed across both datasets highlights its critical role, while the relatively smaller declines from omitting comments or cognition suggest these components contribute less uniquely to overall accuracy. The bars are grouped by dataset and sorted by method label, not by performance, and each bar is labeled with its exact accuracy value.
caption_used: The bar charts illustrate the accuracy percentages for different methods on the PHEME and PolitiFact datasets. Each chart contains six bars representing the categories: 'Ours,' 'w/o comments,' 'w/o text,' 'w/o select,' 'w/o emotion,' and 'w/o cognition,' placed along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled 'Accuracy (%),' uses a linear scale ranging from 75% to 95% with tick intervals of 2.5%. In the PHEME chart, the 'Ours' method achieves the highest accuracy at approximately 89.84%, followed closely by 'w/o select' at 89.80%. The 'w/o text' method shows a significant decline, reaching only 75.10%, the lowest value in the dataset. In the PolitiFact chart, the 'Ours' method again demonstrates the highest accuracy at 90.57%, while 'w/o comments' and 'w/o cognition' exhibit similar performance at 85.85% and 85.74%, respectively. The results suggest that removing text features has the most detrimental impact on accuracy, while the exclusion of comments and cognition leads to comparable performance levels across both datasets.
